newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic says FDA clears 2 new drug pumps.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic says FDA clears 2 new drug pumps.

text.p: Medtronic Inc said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared for commercial marketing two new, thinner models of its SynchroMed implantable drug infusion system.

The new infusion pumps expand access for children and thinner adults to drug therapies for two conditions -- severe spasticity often associated with cerebral palsy, brain injury, multiple sclerosis and spinal cord injury; and pain of malignant and non-malignant origins, Medtronic said.

Implanted just under the skin of the lower abdomen, Medtronic SynchroMed pumps infuse drugs directly into the fluid surrounding the spinal cord through a catheter placed in the intrathecal space, the area surrounding the spinal cord.

The new SynchroMed pumps -- models 8616-10 and 8617-10 -- are 0.85 of an inch thick, or 20 percent thinner than earlier models. The thinner pumps are expected to make intrathecal therapies more accessible and more comfortable for smaller patients.
